ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the graph of the quadratic function $y_{1}=-x^{2}+bx+c$ intersects with the graph of the linear function $y_{2}=kx+2$ at points $A(-1, 3)$ and $B(4, m)$. In order for $y_{1}<y_{2}$, what is the range of values for $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: Since $y_1 < y_2$, \\
it follows that the range of $x$ for which the line is above the parabola is, \\
according to the graph, when $x < -1$ or $x > 4$, \\
therefore $x < -1$ or $x > 4$, \\
hence, the answer is:$\boxed{ x<-1 or x>4}$.
